title: GLP-1 Bridge is Here. How Latent Helps
summary: Medicare's GLP-1 Bridge is the largest medication-access expansion in a decade. A Latent working paper on how health system pharmacy teams meet the new demand.

## Let's talk about how Latent can help your pharmacy.


The Bridge raises the volume for everyone. Get in touch and we'll walk you through how Latent handles the medication-access work alongside your team, on your terms.


[Get in touch with our team](https://www.latenthealth.com/partners#demo)


This paper was written by Clay Coleman with a clinician's read, and built with the same system it describes: a working draft, routed, reviewed, and improved with the same tools. We held every number to its source. Where the workforce evidence was still firming up, we said so. Every patient here, M. Torres included, is synthetic, used only to illustrate the work. No real patient data appears.


Frequently asked


### Common questions about the GLP-1 Bridge


What is Medicare's GLP-1 Bridge?


As of July 1, 2026, Medicare covers GLP-1 medicines for those who meet the Bridge's clinical criteria, usually an obesity diagnosis alongside a qualifying comorbidity. For two decades a 2003 statute locked these patients out. The cash price they faced was more than $1,000 a month. Under the Bridge it is $50.


Why is the Bridge hard for pharmacy teams?


The same medicine, for the same patient, can route two ways, and the answer is not printed on either form. If the basis is obesity plus a comorbidity, it must go on the separate Bridge form, which routes to the CMS central processor at a $50 copay. If a non-obesity indication qualifies, such as type 2 diabetes or sleep apnea, it routes to the patient's Part D plan. Only a chart read tells you which path is correct.


How does Latent help with Bridge cases?


Latent reads the chart, finds the obesity diagnosis and the qualifying comorbidity, rules out the cardiovascular overlap that would route the case to Part D instead, and recommends the right path with its reasoning attached. A read that used to wait on a pharmacist now takes seconds.


Does Latent make the final decision?


No. Latent is assistive today by design. It routes the case and shows its reasoning, and the pharmacist makes the final call.


What results are Latent partners already seeing?


Across Latent's partners, clinicians on the platform handle about twice the patient capacity with the same team, more than 60 health systems are live including half of the top 20 in the U.S., more than 2 million patients a year are accessing medications faster, and medication denials are down more than 30 percent.
